record.original_question: Show that each quasiconformal mapping of Rn onto Rn has a quasiconformal extension to Rn+1 . This has been established by Ahlfors when n = 2 and by Carleson when n = 3. (F. W. Gehring)

evidence.quote: Show that each quasiconformal mapping of Rn onto Rn has a quasiconformal extension to Rn+1 . This has been established by Ahlfors when n = 2 and by Carleson when n = 3. (F. W. Gehring)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A homeomorphism f: R^n → R^n (n ≥ 2) is called K-quasiconformal if f belongs to the Sobolev space W^{1,n}_{loc}(R^n, R^n) and its differential Df(x) satisfies |Df(x)|^n ≤ K · J_f(x) almost everywhere, where J_f denotes the Jacobian determinant. Equivalently, f is quasiconformal if the linear dilatation H(x,f) = limsup_{r→0} (max_{|y-x|=r}|f(y)-f(x)|)/(min_{|y-x|=r}|f(y)-f(x)|) is uniformly bounded on R^n.

Identify R^n with the hyperplane R^n × {0} ⊂ R^{n+1}. Prove that for every n ≥ 2 and every quasiconformal homeomorphism f: R^n → R^n, there exists a quasiconformal homeomorphism F: R^{n+1} → R^{n+1} whose restriction to R^n × {0} coincides with f.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved in full generality by P. Tukia and J. Väisälä in "Quasiconformal extension from dimension n to n+1," Annals of Mathematics 115 (1982), 331–348, who proved that every quasiconformal self-map of R^n extends to a quasiconformal self-map of R^{n+1}. Earlier cases were handled by Ahlfors (n=2) and Carleson (n=3).

status_evidence.title: Quasiconformal extension from dimension n to n+1
status_evidence.snippet: Tukia and Väisälä, Annals of Mathematics 115 (1982), proves quasiconformal extension from R^n to R^{n+1} for all n.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved for all n by Tukia and Väisälä (1982).
